issues.body: `COND_ATOMS` still accepts `!?inputs.<arbitrary-name>`, and `condition_is_live` proves only atom syntax plus distinct context paths. It never checks the input declarations or admitted values of the workflow being inspected. Thus replacing the worker upload condition with `${{ !inputs.target_repo && steps.bundle.outcome == 'success' }}` is certified even though `target_repo` is a required non-empty string for admitted runs, making the upload unreachable while the ordering verdict remains `ordered`. No added fixture exercises this schema-induced contradiction.
issues.fix_hint: Restrict conditions to the exact known-live expressions shipped by these two upload steps, or make validation workflow-aware and prove each input atom and polarity satisfiable under the declared/admitted input contract. Add a named negative fixture for `!inputs.target_repo` and demonstrate that mutating the live worker condition to that expression makes the live ordering assertion fail.
issues.title: Negated required inputs are still accepted as proven-live conditions

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 5 leaves the round-4 blocker materially unchanged. `_upload_step_line` still treats any syntactically valid negated `inputs.<name>` atom as satisfiable without consulting either workflow's declared inputs or their admitted values. Both live workflows declare `target_repo` required, yet `${{ !inputs.target_repo && steps.bundle.outcome == 'success' }}` remains accepted and can make the upload unreachable while `_seal_before_target_code` reports `ordered`. The added negative fixtures cover language-level constants, duplicate paths, and wrapper syntax, but still omit this workflow-schema contradiction. Progress is therefore stagnant.
